row.evidence: Evernote's Enterprise page says Enterprise administrators can set up SSO and SCIM; the compare-plans table only ticks SSO on the Enterprise columns (Flexible, Unlimited), and upgrading to Enterprise is via contact sales.
row.notes: Starter ($99/yr, about $8.25/mo) and Advanced ($249.99/yr, about $20.83/mo) are individual (single-user) plans, so the only multi-user tier is Enterprise (Contact Sales; the compare-plans table shows it as Flexible and Unlimited columns). team_plan is therefore Enterprise and the row is gated because SCIM, SAML SSO and user admin all need that Contact Sales tier. SCIM 1.1 and 2.0 base URLs are documented; SSO must be enabled first; SCIM deletes are ignored (users are deactivated) and deactivated users cannot be reactivated via SCIM. Okta's Evernote Business app ticks SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create and Deactivate; Entra and JumpCloud apps are SSO-only. The legacy EDAM (Thrift) UserStore API has invite/remove/list business-user calls but is deprecated.

scim.notes: SCIM 1.1 is also offered at https://m1.svc.evernote.com/scim/v1/.

endpoints.notes: Only the base URLs are documented; Users is implied by the documented user create/deactivate behaviour.

deprovision.data_retained: Users are deactivated, never deleted; team content stays in the Enterprise account and admins can export a deactivated user's notebooks one at a time.

limitations.text: DELETE requests are ignored; users are only deactivated.
Deactivated users cannot be reactivated via SCIM.
A new user cannot reuse the username of a previously deactivated user.

user_api.notes: Legacy EDAM Cloud API (Thrift RPC), marked deprecated. Business-membership calls need an auth token with privileges to manage Evernote Business membership, so they only apply to Enterprise accounts, which is also the only multi-user tier (hence api_tax false).

capabilities.notes: removeFromBusiness removes a user from the business (only users invited via external provisioning); update is limited to the identifying email address.

endpoints.purpose: Invite a user to join an Evernote Business account
Remove a user from an Evernote Business account
Change the email address that identifies a business user

limitations.text: The EDAM API and SDKs are deprecated and no longer actively developed.

okta.notes: OIN 'Evernote Business' app: SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create and Deactivate are checked (read from page markup). A separate OIN 'Evernote' app is SWA-only.

onelogin.notes: Evernote's SSO article names OneLogin as a SAML partner but no OneLogin provisioning guide was found.
